A lone Orange is not a full monopoly. Base rent is only $14. It blocks p3 from completing a set, but they do not own other oranges yet. It could serve as trade bait later.

I decided to bid $228. The current high bid is still below my stated ceiling of $235-240, so raising by the minimum is consistent with my prior plan. I rejected the idea of dropping out now or bidding higher to test p3's resolve.

The premium is only about 27% over list price.

I will bid the minimum $228. I have set a hard stop at $235. If p3 bids $229 or higher, I will drop out.

I am now unsure whether to bid the minimum or drop out. The war seems pointless. I will think about winning the game.

The $228 cash difference matters more for future auctions of properties actually needed. My light-blue plan is stronger: I already own Vermont, so completing the set with Oriental and Connecticut is cheaper than finishing an Orange set.

I have enough cash to buy the other light blues even after paying $228. Liquidity is not the constraint. I will bid the minimum $228 and then drop out. This signals that I am near my limit.
